ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=80^\circ$, $\angle C=70^\circ$. If $\triangle ABC$ is folded along $EF$, with point $A$ falling on $A'$ inside the shape, what is the measure of $\angle 1+\angle 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=80^\circ$ and $\angle C=70^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle A=180^\circ−\angle B−\angle C=180^\circ−80^\circ−70^\circ=30^\circ$, \\
hence $\angle A'=30^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle A'EF+\angle A'FE=180^\circ−\angle A'=180^\circ−30^\circ=150^\circ$, \\
since $\triangle AFE$ is created by folding $\triangle A'FE$, \\
thus $\angle AEF+\angle AFE=\angle A'EF+\angle A'FE=180^\circ−\angle A'=150^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle 1+\angle 2=360^\circ−\angle B−\angle C−\left(\angle AEF+\angle AFE\right)=360^\circ−80^\circ−70^\circ−150^\circ=\boxed{60^\circ}$.
